blocks.content: Recognizing examiners' traps is just as crucial as mastering the core syllabus.

rows: Underline key qualifiers during first reading
Read all options thoroughly before marking
Spending 5+ minutes on a complex problem

items: Always re-read questions containing double negatives or negative qualifiers like 'NOT true'.
Verify units of measurement in options before marking the final calculated answer.
Never spend more than 2 minutes on a single question during your first iteration.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Pay close attention to key qualifier words like 'NOT', 'INCORRECT', 'ONLY', and 'ALWAYS' in question stems.
Read all four options completely before selecting an answer, even if the first choice seems correct.
Beware of option traps where factual details are partially true but contextually incorrect.
Avoid getting stuck on single time-sink questions during competitive exam passes.
Double-check units and conversion factors in numerical and data interpretation questions.
